title: Rackflow provisioner playbook (sketch)
body:
DRAFT — Rackflow Provisioner playbook

Purpose and scope:
- Sketch for a rack-level provisioning flow and ops playbook (working name: "rackflow-provisioner").
- Target: on-prem clusters deployed into customer racks that may contain mixed compute (baremetal + vSphere ESXi hosts).
- Goal: repeatable, debuggable bootstrap + day-2 upgrade pattern that integrates with our Terraform modules and minimal operator surface (operatorless by default, optional kubeadm/k0s control plane).

Assumptions / constraints:
- Networking: per-rack L2 (VLAN per-rack), DHCP + PXE from a local provisioner VM (or a BMC that supports PXE relay).
- Storage: local disks for worker nodes; for stateful workloads we prefer external SAN/CSI (vSphere or iSCSI).
- Control plane: single rack clusters and multi-rack clusters supported. etcd topology: rack-aware 3/5 node layout recommended.
- Security: customer-managed KMS for TLS certs; we only push bootstrap tokens and short-lived certs via the provisioner.

Component overview (high level):
- rackflow-provisioner (stateless controller running in a small VM or container on admin host):
  - DHCP/iPXE templates + TFTP/Casper-like image serving
  - iSCSI/Ansible hooks for disk partitioning (optional)
  - API for allocating node profiles (role=control/worker/bastion) to MACs/UUIDs
- terraform modules: tf-rackflow/provisioner, tf-rackflow/network, tf-rackflow/dns
- bootstrap artifacts: ignition/kubeadm user-data, minimal image (alpine+systemd), cloud-init shim for vSphere

Key design choices (rationale):
- Operatorless bootstrap: use kubeadm/k0s + plain systemd units to avoid adding another cluster-scoped operator during bootstrap. Simpler to reason about on airgapped installs.
- iPXE layering: primary boot chain will attempt local disk, then iPXE/PXE to network image, then fallback to vSphere template if PXE fails. This handles hybrid racks with bursting to virtual hosts.
- Rack-aware etcd placement: prefer control-plane nodes spread across racks; if single-rack, use odd number; provide an automated etcd backup to NFS or S3-compatible object store per cluster.

Sequence: provisioning happy path (condensed)
1) Pre-step: TF apply for network + provisioner VM
   - terraform apply -var-file=prod-rack.tfvars 
   - Provisioner VM receives ssh key + env secrets (KMS-unwrapped by operator)
2) Register hardware inventory
   - Use MAC or BMC UUID mapping to logical inventory in tf-rackflow/provisioner
   - Example: POST /allocate {mac: 00:11:22:33:44:55, profile: control-3} -> returns iPXE tag
3) PXE boot flow
   - iPXE script mounts a tiny initramfs from provisioner and runs the ignition/kubeadm user-data pull
   - The initramfs performs disk wipe (if profile says ephemeral) or partitions for final layout (for stateful nodes)
4) Control plane bootstrap (first control node)
   - kubeadm init --config=/etc/kubeadm/control-config.yaml
   - Save join tokens/certs to provisioner vault (short expiry)
   - After 3 control nodes join, run etcd snapshot to offsite storage
5) Worker join sequence
   - Workers pull latest runtime metrics image, join with taints based on profile
6) Post-provisioning tasks
   - Apply CNI manifest (we recommend Calico with IPPool per rack for predictable routing)
   - Install local node-exporter, filebeat -> push to central observability (or push gateway)

Terraform module notes (tf-rackflow/provisioner):
- Variables to include (recommended):
  - provisioner_image (string), provisioner_vm_cpu, provisioner_vm_memory, dhcp_range, tftp_root, bootstrap_bucket, admin_ssh_pubkey
- State backend: use remote state (consul or s3) and lock by rack id to avoid concurrent conflicting applies that reassign MACs
- Example minimal HCL (sketch):
  module "provisioner" {
    source = "git::ssh://git@github.com/redwood-inference/tf-rackflow.git//provisioner"
    rack_id = "rack-23-eu"
    dhcp_range = "10.10.23.10-10.10.23.250"
    admin_ssh_pubkey = file("~/.ssh/id_rsa.pub")
  }

- Notes: keep provisioning secrets out of TF state if possible; write ephemeral tokens to secure vault via provisioner init script instead.

Upgrade plan (control-plane and kubelet upgrades) — recommended practice:
- Phased canary rotation (preflight checklist)
  - Collect: node-exporter/K8s metrics (kubelet version, restarts, eviction counts), running critical pods count, PV health
  - Snapshot etcd (automated) -> store snapshot with incremental retention 7/30/90
  - Validate disk space on /var/lib/kubelet and /var/lib/etcd on control nodes
- Control plane upgrade (kubeadm/k8s):
  1) Pick one control node (canary) in rack with least serving load. cordon + drain non-critical control-plane sidecars (if any).
  2) kubeadm upgrade apply vX.Y.Z on canary control node. restart kubelet. wait 10–20 min and validate cluster health (kubectl get cs, kubectl get nodes).
  3) If stable, proceed one-by-one with remaining control nodes. Ensure etcd cluster health after each node rejoin.
- Worker upgrade:
  - orchestrate by taint-based rolling: cordon -> drain (with --ignore-daemonsets) -> upgrade kubelet binary (or replace image for k0s) -> uncordon
  - batch size: start small (5% of workers or 2 nodes) and increase if no regressions

Data-plane PV considerations for upgrade/rotation:
- For local PVs: prefer evacuation + recreate pattern. If workloads use local-only storage, schedule maintenance windows.
- For CSI-backed volumes (vSphere, Ceph, iSCSI): verify volume detach/attach timeouts and have retry policies in K8s storage class.

Runbook snippets & helpful commands (paste into terminal when debugging)
- Check provisioner allocations: curl -sS http://provisioner.local/api/v1/inventory | jq .
- Trigger remote PXE chain for MAC: curl -X POST http://provisioner.local/api/v1/actions/reboot -d '{"mac":"00:11:22:33:44:55"}'
- Grab kubeadm tokens from provisioner vault (short lived): vault kv get -field=token secret/racks/rack-23/cluster-foo
- Quick etcd health: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 endpoint status --cert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.crt --key=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/peer.key --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt

Common failure modes and mitigations:
- Node stuck in PXE loop: check TFTP logs (provisioner/service) and iPXE script; common cause: wrong iPXE variable for image path after retries.
- Hardware NIC mismatch (bios naming vs OS): implement udev rules based on MACs in initramfs so device name drift doesn't break partition scripts.
- Kubelet failing after upgrade: check cgroups driver mismatch; validate container runtime version and systemd config.
- Persistent volume attach timeouts during rotation: increase attach/detach timeouts in CSI driver and stagger node rotations.

Operational checklist (pre-flight)
- [ ] etcd snapshot done and verified offsite
- [ ] Observability: dashboards for pod restarts, node conditions, PV attach latency
- [ ] Backups for critical cluster secrets (KMS + etcd backups)
- [ ] Terraform plan reviewed, remote state locked, and approvals in PR
- [ ] Runbook and rollback steps reviewed with on-call

Open questions / TODOs
- Do we standardize on kubeadm or k0s for all customer installs? k0s is simpler for airgap but kubeadm provides more control for upgrades (tradeoffs). TODO: collect telemetry on how often operatorless bootstrap works without intervention (owner: Michael Chen).
- Policy around persistent workloads in single-rack clusters (SLA/compensation).
- Automation: add a TF null_resource to trigger an airgapped image build and SHA verification step before update.

References and tickets
- Design confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Rackflow+Design
- Infra provisioning PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra-provisioning/pull/412
- Related jira: JIRA-RI-2897 (opaque inventory mapping + DHCP lease handoff)

Notes to self:
- Keep provisioner as small as possible; prefer simple HTTP API + file templates rather than large orchestration stacks.
- Try to capture more real-world timings (PXE->kube ready) per rack; add metrics to provisioner for boot latency distribution.

If this sketch looks reasonable, next steps:
- Turn selected sections into a more formal playbook (replace placeholders with exact commands, cert rotation steps, and acceptance criteria).
- Create tf-rackflow/provisioner module skeleton and a tiny demo repo that spins a VM + serves a test iPXE image so SREs can test in lab.

-- end of sketch --
